human_text: The Welsh government is more than halfway through a £4.6m five-year programme to immunise badgers in north Pembrokeshire.Infection rates have fallen across Wales, but Christianne Glossop said it was too early to say whether it has had "additional benefit".Dr Glossop was speaking ahead of a worldwide conference on TB control.It will be held in Cardiff on Monday."The programme is for five years," she told BBC's Sunday Politics Wales."We've completed two years and we're now well into year three, and so the results are by no means available yet."TB infection rates fell across Wales over the last 12 months, she said."The reduction in north Pembrokeshire is in line with the national reduction, so right now, we have no evidence that the vaccination programme in badgers is delivering an additional benefit - and we wouldn't expect to see any evidence at this stage either," she said.In 2012 and 2013, 2,776 badgers were trapped and vaccinated in the Intensive Action Area (IAA), which also takes in parts of Ceredigion and Carmarthenshire, at a cost of more than £1.8m.But Dr Glossop said that the wider TB eradication programme cost £28m last year alone, most of which was spent on testing cattle, biosecurity and compensating farmers."You've always got to have the balance here between all the different elements of the programme, making sure that you're tackling all sources of infection," she said.The vaccination programme was announced by Labour ministers in 2012 when they abandoned the previous coalition government's intention to cull badgers in the IAA.

direct_prompt: **Owl Art Auction Raises £508,000 for Charity**BIRMINGHAM, England (AP) — An auction of giant decorated owl statues that were part of a city-wide art exhibition has raised 508,000 pounds ($680,000) for charity.The 100 owls, each designed by a different artist, were displayed around Birmingham for 10 weeks before being auctioned off on Thursday. The proceeds from the auction will benefit the Birmingham Children’s Hospital Charity.The highest bid of the night was 30,000 pounds ($40,000) for an owl decorated with flowers and butterflies by artist Claire Rolinson. Other owls sold for prices ranging from 5,000 pounds ($6,700) to 15,000 pounds ($20,000).“We are absolutely thrilled with the amount of money that was raised at the auction,” said Lisa Stalley, the hospital charity’s corporate fundraising manager. “This money will make a real difference to the lives of the children we care for.”The auction was organized by the Big Hoot, a public art project that brings together artists, businesses, and the community to create a unique and inspiring experience.The Big Hoot has raised more than 1.7 million pounds ($2.3 million) for charity since it began in 2015.

human_text: The Endeavour project has bought a former German harbour ferry for £1 with the hope of raising £3m to restore the 59-year-old rusting vessel.A service used to link Liverpool with the Welsh resort, while en route to the Isle of Man, 30 years ago."The money is coming from some private investors," said restorer Steve Payne."We have some fund-raising ourselves and then we've had some bequests come in as well."The 55-metre long vessel, first launched in Hamburg in 1958, has been rusting in Liverpool docks since 1994 when an attempt to turn her into a floating bar on Liverpool's famous Albert Dock failed.Enthusiasts, headed by Mr Payne, saved her from scrap in 2016 with the dream of offering three-hour summer day trips for up to 450 people from Liverpool to Llandudno.The Endeavour's two diesel engines will have to be refurbished while the lifeboats have been sent to Norway for an overhaul.Many of the ship's fittings need replacing and even the ship's wheel has been stolen."If we were to build a ship this size, new at the moment, we'd be looking around £25m-£30m," said Mr Payne, secretary of the Liverpool and North Wales Steam Ship Company."We have the basis of a very, very good ship here."Mr Payne is confident the new limited company can meet the health and safety requirements necessary to allow The Endeavour leave her berth in Liverpool's Canada Dock again.The Endeavour has no history of sailing in British waters but Mr Payne believes she is the ideal ship for traditional summer day trippers."You can't find ships like this any more," he said."There's not a major UK connection but we want to establish a new connection for this ship so children can have a chance to experience this in 25 years time the way their grandparents did."

summary: Gareth Southgate should be appointed England manager "as soon as possible" and be given the same contract as predecessor Sam Allardyce, says former Three Lions defender Danny Mills.
direct_prompt: Gareth Southgate, the current England Under-21s manager, should be appointed as the new England manager as soon as possible, according to former Three Lions defender Danny Mills. Mills believes that Southgate deserves the same contract as his predecessor Sam Allardyce. Allardyce resigned as England manager after just 67 days in charge, following a scandal involving his conduct in a Daily Telegraph investigation. Southgate is thought to be the leading candidate to replace Allardyce on a permanent basis, having impressed as interim manager in England's World Cup qualifier against Malta last month. The FA are expected to make an announcement about the new manager in the next few days. Southgate, who won 57 caps for England, has been in charge of the Under-21s since 2013 and led them to the semi-finals of the European Championship in the summer. He has also worked as the England senior team's assistant manager and has been praised for his work with young players. Mills, who played 19 times for England, believes that Southgate is the right man to lead England into the 2018 World Cup in Russia. He said: "Gareth is the outstanding candidate. He's won things at youth level with England, he knows what the job entails. He is young and hungry. He has got time on his side and he can build for the future." Southgate has been linked with a number of Premier League clubs in recent years, but he has always stated his desire to manage England. He is thought to be keen on the idea of being given a long-term contract, which would allow him to plan for the future. The FA are keen to appoint a manager who will be in charge for the long term and they believe that Southgate is the right man to do that.
prompt_few_shot: Former England defender Danny Mills believes Gareth Southgate should be appointed as the permanent manager of the national team “as soon as possible”. Southgate, currently in charge on an interim basis, has won two and drawn two of his four games in charge. Mills thinks the Football Association should act quickly to tie the former defender down to a similar contract to that of predecessor Sam Allardyce, who was sacked after just 67 days in charge.“I think the FA need to confirm him as soon as possible and give him the same contract as Sam Allardyce,” Mills told BBC Radio 5 live. “He’s not just in charge until the end of the season, is he? He’s in charge for four years with a view to the next World Cup. Give him the contract now and get it sorted because it takes away any uncertainty.”Southgate took over from Allardyce after the former England boss was caught up in a newspaper sting that led to his departure. The 46-year-old has since overseen wins over Malta and Scotland and a draw against Slovenia in World Cup qualifying, as well as a friendly draw with Spain.Mills believes Southgate has done enough to warrant the job on a permanent basis. “I think it’s a no-brainer,” he said. “He’s been a breath of fresh air. The players seem to enjoy working under him. Results have been good. Performances have been good. There’s been a real change in the way England play. He’s brought back that enjoyment, that freedom of expression.”The former Manchester City and Leeds defender also believes Southgate should continue to experiment with his team and tactics. “I don’t think he needs to change a great deal,” he said. “We’ve been talking for a long time about England having an identity and being a certain way. But if you do that, you’ll always be found out. Other teams will work you out. What Gareth’s done is he’s changed the system and played different players in different positions. The players have responded to that.

human_text: Craig Logan, 22, died at the Ayrshire facility in February 2015 after he became trapped while checking a fault that had halted the crane.At Kilmarnock Sheriff Court, operator Clydeport pleaded guilty to health and safety breaches.These included failing to make risk assessments and ensure safe working systems from July 2014 until the death.The lapses also included failing to ensure the north unloader crane cab was electrically isolated so it could not restart unexpectedly, or to provide means for workers to communicate with each other.Clydeport also failed to provide access to a lift and sling system so staff did not have to move the cab physically, or identify risks of injury from freeing the cab when it was stuck, or falling from the boom.The court heard that the tragedy happened the day before a safety assessment was due to be made, following the departure of key managers with responsibility for health and safety.Sheriff Shirley Foran expressed sympathy to Mr Logan's family and said the penalty she had to impose "in no ways reflects the value of his life."Sheriff Foran added that the absence of a qualified risk assessment engineer and health and safety manager for seven to eight months before the incident meant the company "knew they were thereby exposed."The assessment due the day after Mr Logan's death was the "most bitter of ironies", Sheriff Foran added.A spokesman for Clydeport, which has previous health and safety convictions, said outside court: "We failed to meet the very high standards we set ourselves and a young man tragically paid with his life, for which we are sincerely sorry."The failures which contributed to this tragic accident should have been avoided and indeed, a full external health and safety review was already due to start the day after Craig died."Since the accident, we have comprehensively reviewed our approach to health and safety at Hunterston to do everything possible to ensure there can be no repeat."

It includes a hospital and retirement homes.Alex Burkenshaw, senior carer at Queens Residential Home, said the 39 residents were a "hardy bunch"."We are lucky as the home has one electric oven, so we can still cook meals," she said."The gas company has been and given us about 10 heaters so we have been able to warm all the lounges."It's more like a four-cardigan day for the residents."Withernsea resident Steve Medcalf criticised the lack of information from the gas company.But he said "great community spirit" meant the town was "pulling together", with the supermarket and cafes helping out."It's cold, but I think everybody's in the same boat," he added.Northern Gas Networks urged residents using electric heaters and hotplates to use electricity "with consideration" to avoid putting "excessive strain on the electricity network". It said it was working with Northern Powergrid to manage the situation.An incident room has been set up on Hull Road playing fields, where heaters are being handed out.Anyone who smells gas should call the National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999.

The company has been working on autonomous vehicle technology for several years, aiming to compete with other major players in the industry.
With this approval, Samsung joins other tech companies such as Waymo and Tesla in the race to develop safe and reliable self-driving cars. The tests will take place on designated roads in South Korea, under strict supervision to ensure the safety of both the drivers and pedestrians.
Samsung's foray into self-driving cars comes as part of its efforts to diversify its business and stay ahead in the rapidly evolving tech industry. Samsung has not yet announced a timeline for when its self-driving cars will be ready for commercial deployment, but the testing phase is a crucial step in the development process. The company will continue to fine-tune its technology and algorithms during the testing phase to ensure optimum performance on the roads.
Overall, the approval for Samsung to begin testing its self-driving cars in South Korea represents a significant step forward for the company and the autonomous vehicle industry as a whole. As technology continues to advance, it will be interesting to see how Samsung's self-driving cars will stack up against the competition in the coming years.

summary: Tottenham have signed defender Davinson Sanchez from Ajax in a reported club record £42m deal, subject to a medical and a work permit.

Tottenham manager Mauricio Pochettino has been keen to strengthen his backline ahead of a challenging Premier League campaign. The signing of Sanchez shows the North London club's ambition to compete at the highest level.

Sanchez's signing is a statement of intent from Tottenham as they aim to challenge for major honors this season. The young defender is excited about the opportunity to play in the Premier League and test himself against some of the best attackers in the world.

Overall, the signing of Davinson Sanchez is a significant boost for Tottenham as they look to build on their impressive performances in recent years. Fans will be eagerly anticipating his debut and hoping that he can help the team achieve success in both domestic and European competitions.

The government's recent demonetization policy, aimed at curbing corruption and tax evasion, is expected to have a short-term impact on growth but is predicted to lead to long-term benefits for the economy.
